title: Hidden Edge 2
content:
If that strike had connected, it might not have brought Nie Mingjue down, but it would have bought them a few precious seconds. Unfortunately, Su She had crammed far too much spiritual energy into the steel during that desperate burst. Pushed way past its breaking point, the blade shattered mid-swing with a loud clang, exploding into jagged fragments.

Nie Mingjue’s bare fist slammed dead into his sternum.

Su She’s brief moment of brilliance vanished in an instant. He didn’t even get the chance to cough up a dying mouthful of blood, let alone spit out a defiant last word. The light in his eyes simply blinked out.

Slumped next to Lan Xichen, Jin Guangyao watched the whole thing happen. Maybe it was the agonizing burn of his severed wrist and the blood pouring from his torn abdomen, or maybe it was something else entirely, but tears welled in the corners of his eyes. Nie Mingjue, however, didn't give him a second to breathe or lick his wounds. Wrenching his arm free, the corpse spun back around, fixing him with a predatory, locked-on glare.

That craggy, unforgiving face bore the exact same harsh, judging sneer from when he was alive—the face Jin Guangyao feared above all else. The sight scared the tears right back into his ducts. His voice hitched in a terrified, trembling plea: "Er-ge..."

Lan Xichen wheeled his sword around, while Wei Wuxian and Lan Wangji scrambled to kick their tempo into overdrive. But once a whistle’s rhythm was broken, picking the thread back up was twice as hard.

Just then, a voice barked from the sidelines: "Wei Wuxian!"

Wei Wuxian blinked. "What?!"

Only after he answered did he realize it was Jiang Cheng calling him. Before he could process the surprise, Jiang Cheng whipped an arm out and hurled an object across the hall. Wei Wuxian caught it on pure reflex.

He looked down. Sleek, polished black bamboo, tipped with a vivid crimson tassel.

The ghost flute, Chenqing!

The familiar, cool weight of the instrument in his grip instantly blasted away all his shock. Without wasting half a thought, he brought it straight to his lips and shouted, "Lan Zhan!"

Lan Wangji gave a slight nod. No words needed.

Zither and flute rang out in seamless unison. The guqin rushed like a subterranean glacial spring, while the flute soared like a wild bird taking flight—one crushing down, the other steering. Tangled beneath the twin assault, Nie Mingjue’s towering frame rocked. Slowly, stubbornly, his heavy boots were pried away from Jin Guangyao.

Step by stiff step, under the absolute grip of the duet, he was marched backward toward that lavish empty coffin a second time. Wei Wuxian and Lan Wangji shadowed him, keeping pace stride for stride. The second the hulking corpse tumbled backward into the pit, both men kicked the discarded lid from opposite ends. The heavy slab of timber launched into the air and slammed down flush over the rim.

Wei Wuxian vaulted onto the top of the coffin with effortless grace. Slipping Chenqing back into his sash with his left hand, he bit clean through his right index finger and dragged his bloody tip across the wood in one fluid, breathtaking stroke. Cursive, dripping blood runes unfurled in a frantic flurry, without a single hitch from start to finish!

Only then did the muffled, beast-like thrashing inside begin to quiet down.

Lan Wangji flattened his palm over the trembling silk strings, silencing the reverberations beneath his fingertips.

Wei Wuxian let out a slow breath, pausing to extend his senses. Confident the brute force underneath had finally been snuffed out, he stood straight and sighed, "Man, what an awful temper."

Perched on the lid, he towered way over everyone else. Lan Wangji stowed his instrument, looking up at him with those quiet, amber-tinted eyes. Wei Wuxian leaned down, couldn't resist, and reached out to give that clean, porcelain cheek a teasing little poke—leaving behind a couple of bright, messy streaks of crimson, whether by accident or purely on purpose.

Lan Wangji didn't swat him away. He just murmured softly, "Come down."

Wei Wuxian grinned and hopped down from the perch, landing flush against Lan Wangji's chest as the man caught him clean.

Things had barely settled down on their end when a chorus of pathetic groans broke out from the other side of the hall.

Nie Huaisang was weeping openly: "Xichen-ge! Please, come check on me! Is my leg still attached to my hip?!"

Lan Xichen hurried over, kneeling down to press a steadying hand over the wound. "Huaisang, calm down. It's fine. The leg isn't severed, it's just a puncture."

Nie Huaisang sounded downright hysterical: "A puncture?! How am I supposed to stay calm over a puncture?! Did it punch clean through?! Xichen-ge, save me, I'm dying!"

Lan Xichen didn't know whether to laugh or cry. "It's really not that deep."

Nie Huaisang kept rolling around on the floorboards anyway, clutching his thigh for dear life. Knowing full well how low the man's pain tolerance was, Lan Xichen fished a small porcelain vial from his robes and pressed it into his trembling palm. "For the pain."

Nie Huaisang scrambled to choke down two pills on the spot, whining through mouthfuls: "How am I this cursed? First that bastard Su Minshan kidnaps me out of nowhere, and then he stabs me on his way out the door! If he wanted me out of the way, he could've just shoved me! What's with pulling cold steel on people..."

Lan Xichen rose and turned around.

Jin Guangyao was slumped against the wall, pale as a ghost, hair falling in loose tangles across a forehead drenched in cold sweat. It was an utter, pitiful mess. The agony from his severed wrist was clearly chewing through him, coaxing faint, ragged whimpers past his clenched teeth. He lifted his lashes to look at Lan Xichen. He didn't utter a word, but the sight of him cradling that bloody stump, paired with that shattered, kicking-dog gaze, made it almost impossible not to feel a twinge of pity.

Lan Xichen watched him for a long moment. With a quiet, conflicted sigh, he reached back into his lapel for more medicine.

"Lan-zongzhu," Wei Wuxian called out.

Lan Xichen paused. "Master Wei, look at him... In this state, he can hardly pull another trick. If we don't staunch the bleeding now, he'll drop dead on these floorboards. There is still too much left unsaid."

"I get it, Lan-zongzhu," Wei Wuxian replied, his tone leveling out. "I'm not saying let him bleed out. I'm telling you to stay on your guard. Better slap a Silence Spell on him while you're at it—don't let him start spinning yarns again."

Lan Xichen gave a solemn nod, turning his gaze back down to the captive. "Jin-zongzhu, you heard him. I suggest you refrain from any unnecessary movements. To be safe, if you so much as twitch, I will not hesitate..." He drew in a sharp breath. "...to take your life."

Jin Guangyao dipped his chin weakly, whispering, "Thank you, Zewu-jun..."

Lan Xichen crouched down, carefully and deliberately dressing the raw stump. Jin Guangyao shivered through the entire process. Seeing his once-dazzling sworn brother reduced to a bloody wreck on the floor left Lan Xichen at a total loss for words, able to do nothing but swallow his sorrow.

Across the room, Wei Wuxian and Lan Wangji strolled back toward the corner. Wen Ning was still sprawled in an awkward heap across Jiang Cheng and Jin Ling. Wei Wuxian carefully hauled him flat onto the flagstones, eyeing the gaping cavity in the fierce corpse's sternum with an exasperated wince. "Well, look at you... What on earth are we supposed to patch this with?"

"Gongzi..." Wen Ning rasped faintly, "is it bad...?"

"Nah, not bad," Wei Wuxian said casually. "It's not like you're actually using those organs anyway. It just looks like hell."

"I don't need to look pretty..." Wen Ning mumbled.

Jiang Cheng stayed dead silent, while Jin Ling looked like he was biting his tongue so hard it might bleed.

Over by the pillar, Lan Xichen was wrapping the final layer of gauze. Seeing Jin Guangyao on the verge of passing out from the sheer agony, the urge to discipline him melted away into reluctant mercy. He turned his head: "Huaisang, hand me that vial from earlier."

Having popped the pills, Nie Huaisang had already tucked the bottle back into his coat. "Oh, right! Sure!" He fumbled through his lapels, pulling the vial free. He held it out toward Lan Xichen—and his pupils violently shrank into pinpricks.

"Xichen-ge, behind you!" he shrieked in absolute terror.

Lan Xichen had never truly let his guard down; his nerves were pulled tight as a bowstring. Catching the raw panic contorting Nie Huaisang's face, cold dread spiked down his spine. Without a single microsecond of hesitation, he whipped Shuoyue from its scabbard and drove the blade backward blind.

The clean steel drove straight through Jin Guangyao’s chest, punching clean out his back.

Jin Guangyao froze, his face a mask of utter, dazed shock.

The sudden turn of violence knocked the wind out of the entire room. Wei Wuxian sprang to his feet, barking, "What happened?!"

"I... I saw..." Nie Huaisang stammered, teeth chattering wildly. "San-ge... no, Jin-zongzhu reached his hand behind his back! I thought he was about to... to pull something..."

Jin Guangyao looked down at the blade impaling his sternum, his lips parting, desperate to defend himself. But bound beneath the Silence Spell, he was completely robbed of a voice.

Wei Wuxian’s instincts fired—something about this felt horribly off.

Before he could step in, Jin Guangyao heaved a violent, jagged cough, spraying a mouthful of dark gore across the tiles. His voice tore out in a hoarse, cracked rasp:

"Lan Xichen!"

He had forcefully blown right through the Gusu Lan silencing charm with raw, agonizing willpower.

His body was a map of catastrophic ruins—a blistered, melted left hand, a severed right wrist, a torn flank, drenched head to toe in blood. He hadn't even had the strength to sit upright a second ago, yet pushed by some violent, dying adrenaline, he hauled himself up onto his own two feet.

"Lan Xichen!" he snarled again, his voice dripping venom.

Lan Xichen looked utterly gutted, his eyes hollowed out by grief. "Jin-zongzhu. I warned you. If you moved, I would show no mercy."

Jin Guangyao spat a mouthful of bloody phlegm right onto the floor. "Yes! You warned me! But did I make a move?! Did I?!"

The man had spent a lifetime wearing a mask of buttery-smooth, courtly grace, yet here he was, baring his fangs like a feral street brawler. Seeing him unravel this violently made Lan Xichen pause, a flicker of doubt nudging him to look back toward Nie Huaisang.

Jin Guangyao let out a manic, hacking laugh. "Enough! What are you looking at him for?! Stop looking! What do you expect to find? I spent decades by his side and never saw through him! Huaisang... oh, you played your part brilliantly, didn't you?!"

Nie Huaisang looked struck dumb, shrinking back as if terrified out of his wits by the wild accusation.

Jin Guangyao’s jaw clenched so hard his teeth creaked. "To think... I actually ended up ruined by your hands..."

He lurched forward, dragging his feet toward Nie Huaisang, but with a cold length of spiritual steel pinning his lungs, every millimeter forward spiked a sickening wave of agony. Lan Xichen couldn't bring himself to twist the blade for a kill, but pulling the sword out risked a fatal hemorrhage.

"Don't move!" Lan Xichen shouted, panicked.

Jin Guangyao had reached his limit anyway. His bare hand clamped around the edge of the blade embedded in his ribs, anchoring his stance as he coughed up another dark knot of blood. "What a glorious 'Head-Shaker'! What a masterpiece! No wonder... Hiding your claws for all these years, you really put in the work, didn't you?!"

Nie Huaisang trembled violently, practically melting into the floorboards. "Xichen-ge, you have to believe me! I really saw him reach—"

"You!" Jin Guangyao roared, his face contorting into something demonic.

He threw his weight forward again, driving the blade another inch deeper into his chest. Lan Xichen barked, "Stand down!"

Lan Xichen had walked into far too many of Jin Guangyao's traps in his life; natural paranoia whispered that this was just another calculated deflection, a desperate bid to turn the tables after getting caught red-handed.

Jin Guangyao read the doubt in his eyes like an open book. A bitter, venomous laugh tore from his throat.

"Lan Xichen! I've spun a thousand lies and ruined countless lives! Just like you said—killing my father, my brother, my wife, my son, my master, my friends! What wickedness under the sun haven't I had a hand in?!"

He dragged in a jagged, rattling breath, his voice dropping to a gravelly, broken whisper:

"Yet out of the entire damn world, you are the one person I never, ever thought to hurt!"

Lan Xichen went rigid.

Jin Guangyao fought for air, his fingers clawing into the cold flat of Shuoyue, gnashing his teeth through the pain. "...When the Cloud Recesses burned to the ground and you were hunted like an animal, who pulled you out of the fire? When the Gusu Lan Sect rebuilt from the ashes, who moved heaven and earth to pour resources into your halls? Over all these years, when have I ever suppressed your sect?! When haven't I backed you to the absolute hilt?! Aside from locking your spiritual power tonight, when have I ever wronged you or your family?! When did I ever come knocking to demand repayment?!"

The questions rained down like physical blows, and Lan Xichen found himself completely unable to summon another silencing seal.

"Su Minshan gave his life for me today simply because I bothered to remember his name back then," Jin Guangyao sneered, tears cutting through the grime on his face. "And you? Zewu-jun, Sect Leader Lan... In the end, you're just like Nie Mingjue. You can't stand the sight of me. You won't even grant me a single road to live!"

Right on the final word, Jin Guangyao threw his weight violently backward, tearing himself clean off Shuoyue's blade.

"Don't let him run!" Jiang Cheng yelled.

Lan Xichen closed the distance in two strides, snagging him by the collar with zero effort. In his shredded state, Jin Guangyao couldn't have outrun a toddler; even a blindfolded Jin Ling could have wrestled him down. Between the blood loss and the fatal stab through his lungs, he was hardly a threat anymore.

Then it hit Wei Wuxian like a bucket of ice water.

"He's not trying to run!" Wei Wuxian bellowed. "Zewu-jun, get away from him! Now!"

Too late.

The blood pouring from Jin Guangyao’s severed stump had already painted the lacquered wood of the coffin. The crimson trails washed right over the fresh runes Wei Wuxian had drawn, dissolving the wards before slipping through the hairline seam of the lid.

The beast beneath the timber detonated!

The heavy lid exploded into kindling. A massive, pallid hand shot out from the splinters, clamping iron-tight around Jin Guangyao’s throat—while the other lunged straight for Lan Xichen’s windpipe!

Jin Guangyao hadn't been fleeing; he was burning his dying breath to drag Lan Xichen into the pit, dead set on dragging them both straight to hell!

Lan Wangji whipped Bichen forward like a bolt of lightning, the blade screaming through the dark. But a monster like Nie Mingjue didn't give a damn about spiritual swords; even if Bichen struck home, it wouldn't stop those iron claws from crushing Lan Xichen's throat in that split second.

Yet right when the gray fingers were a hair's breadth from snapping his neck, Jin Guangyao’s mangled left hand shoved hard against Lan Xichen's chest, throwing the sect leader clear of the coffin.

In the same breath, Nie Mingjue’s grip hauled Jin Guangyao bodily into the pit, hoisting him into the air by the neck like a ragged, limp doll. The sight was pure, grotesque horror. Jin Guangyao clawed desperately at the iron fingers crushing his throat, writhing in agony, his hair wild and his eyes flaring with rabid, unhinged fury.

He coughed up a lungful of blood, screeching with every drop of life he had left:

"Nie Mingjue, fuck your entire bloodline! You think I'm actually scared of you?! I—"

Crack.

The sound was shockingly crisp, echoing with brutal clarity through the cavernous hall.

A faint, rattling wheeze escaped Jin Guangyao's lips as his head rolled limp.

Jin Ling’s shoulders jerked. He clamped his hands over his ears and squeezed his eyes shut, terrified to look, terrified to hear another sound.
